objective: Establish the identity and documented family of Glasgow-3021, separating sourced facts from tree assertions.

questions.question: Which records prove the subject's identity across events?
questions.answer: A specific daughter-in-law alternative can now be tested. Paterson’s 1866 county history, printed pp. 513–514 (PDF 249–250), says the elder Robert’s eldest son and heir, born 22 May 1811, married Mary-Wilhelmina, daughter of John Campbell of Stonefield, on 11 July 1839; their children include Wilhelmina-Colquhoun. The checked existing bride is Campbell-38211 and groom Robertson-Glasgow-11. A married Mary beside the infant of this same family could be that daughter-in-law rather than another daughter of the household head. This is a new comparison, not an established identification. The age problem remains real: FreeCEN gives Mary 19 in 1841, while Campbell-38211’s public profile gives 1816 and copies an 1851 age 34. The latter original is also unread. The infant’s full name and birth particulars are not established by FreeCEN. Paterson is a compiled family history, not an original marriage entry, and its adjacent Montgreenan descent narrative has known conflicts with the separately held court evidence. Do not transfer the book’s explicit John Campbell parentage to Glasgow-3021 before identifying the two Marys. Retain the selected Robert Robertson father at 45%, Jane’s father at 78%, all mother/vital fields and separate profiles; no father replacement, merge or confidence improvement is recorded. Checked candidate: https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Campbell-38211

research_state.last_test: The original 1841 Holly Walk census image has now been inspected through Findmypast: HO107/1135/14, folio 11, printed page 15, Leamington Priors. Robert is 65; Mary is entered with the Glasgow surname repeated by ditto and a Scotland birthplace mark. Mary’s final age digit remains ambiguous between 17 and 19: Findmypast transcribes 17, FreeCEN 19. Ann’s age also has an unresolved final digit (40/44; both providers transcribe 40). The schedule has no relationship column. These are readings of one census, not three independent family witnesses.
research_state.next_test: Inspect original 1851 census for Campbell-38211 and Robertson-Glasgow-11, then their 11 July 1839 marriage; compare age, full name, infant and residence. Do not repeat the completed 1841 access/image test.
research_state.review_conclusion: The original does not prove Mary was Robert’s daughter or identify her with Mary Wilhelmina Campbell. Its 17/19 age reading still conflicts with the comparison bride’s 1816 birth and copied 1851 age 34. Keep that daughter-in-law comparison unselected and the existing father at 45%; Jane’s father remains 78%. No parent, identity, mother or vital-field change is made. The existing 1804 France birth fields remain unverified and conflict with the census, rather than being confirmed by it. A full original 1851 household and the 1839 marriage remain the discriminating identity tests.
